elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained carve-out: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate". The "financially responsible" qualifier narrows the carve-out slightly but the affiliate right survives without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted "or to a successor in interest, upon written notice to the other party" into the no-approval carve-out; "successor in interest" ordinarily captures a merger/acquisition/asset-sale successor, though the preferred position enumerates those triggers expressly.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The clause remains symmetrical ("Neither party ... without the prior written approval of the other party, ... except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest"), so TrueLink may assign to an affiliate or successor without our consent. Preferred would require the carve-outs to run only in Customer's favour.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted "not to be unreasonably withheld" immediately after "the prior written approval of the other party"; it applies mutually and therefore to our consent to a TrueLink assignment.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor bar appears anywhere in the rendered Section 15; indeed the new mutual successor carve-out lets TrueLink transfer to a successor (potentially a competitor) with no consent at all.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: Section 15 contains no "deemed an assignment"/change-of-control language, and the finding records that the term and termination provisions (p0078-p0079) contain no change-of-control trigger or re-pricing right, so nothing needed deleting.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign ... without the prior written approval of the other party ... except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest" - the carve-out is expressed mutually ("Neither party" / "the other party").

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in interest, upon written notice to the other party" - the notice condition sits on the carve-out that includes successor assignments.
Original consent gate preserved verbatim: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party".

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "without the prior written approval of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld" - the absolute veto identified in the original is now qualified by a reasonableness standard.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the rendered Section 15 delivers a mutual successor carve-out, a written-notice condition on that carve-out, a retained consent gate for all other assignments, and a not-unreasonably-withheld standard on that consent. The claimed 'deviation' status and fallback target are supported.

Preferred level is not complete and is correctly not claimed: TrueLink keeps the same affiliate/successor carve-outs (so it can assign without our consent), and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. To reach preferred the drafter would have to make the carve-outs one-way in Customer's favour and add wording such as 'and in no event to a competitor of Customer'.

Drafting nit to tighten if desired: 'upon written notice to the other party' is positioned at the end of the combined carve-out and can be read as attaching a notice condition to the pre-existing affiliate carve-out as well. If we want the affiliate right left wholly unconditional, recast as '... to a financially responsible affiliate, or, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in interest.'

Residual commercial point (not a fallback defect): 'successor in interest' is undefined and now also benefits TrueLink, so a TrueLink competitor-acquirer could take the contract without our consent. If that is a concern, the preferred-level competitor exclusion is the repair; adding it would exceed the minimal fallback edit chosen here.

Minimality holds: only three insertions were made ('not to be unreasonably withheld', 'or to a successor in interest', 'upon written notice to the other party'), the existing affiliate carve-out and the mutual consent architecture are retained, and no operative term is duplicated.
Intent is preserved: no change to term, termination, pricing or remedies, and no change-of-control trigger was introduced or needed to be deleted, consistent with the finding's survey of p0078-p0080.
